title: The “inert” noble gases can form compounds after all
body: For decades chemists assumed noble gases like neon, argon and xenon couldn’t react, because their outer electron shells are full. In 1962 Neil Bartlett noticed that platinum hexafluoride could rip an electron off an oxygen molecule, and that xenon gives up an electron almost as easily. He mixed xenon with it and made the first credible noble gas compound. Many xenon compounds are now known, and in 2000 chemists even made a compound of argon.
